benchmark: P2 AMD node, node side: VA-API encode on a Radeon 780M, GPU clocks on auto vs the video clocks forced high

node.host: mini-titan.lan (Proxmox VE 9.2, kernel 7.0.14-23-pve), LXC container made by deploy/proxmox/create-node.sh
node.driver: amdgpu; radeonsi and RADV from Mesa 26.0.8 (the streamer and Steam images)
node.gpu_shared_with: nothing else; the same GPU draws the app

content: Steam's Big Picture (gamescope on RADV) at the home screen; gamescope committed 190-290 frames/s, the compositor had new damage on 16-36 of the 60 encode ticks a second

stream.path: WebTransport to the Claude app's browser pane (Chromium 152), hidden

note: Streamer-side encoder statistics (the 10 s 'encoder µs p50/p99' log). The pane was hidden, so no browser-side timings are included. Each run is 10 s; the levels were set on the host with power_dpm_force_performance_level and pp_dpm_vclk/pp_dpm_dclk and put back to auto after.

runs.gpu_clocks: auto (sclk 800 MHz, vclk 800 MHz, dclk 800 MHz)
high (everything at its top: sclk 2700 MHz)
manual: vclk 2400 MHz, dclk 2057 MHz, sclk left at 800 MHz
deploy/node/host/73-cha-amd-video-clocks.rules applied by udev (manual; vclk and dclk at their top step)

conclusion: On auto the video engine stays at its lowest clock under a 60 fps stream and HEVC at 1440p takes 7 ms to encode; with the video clocks alone forced high it takes 3.25 ms (p99 3.4), the 3D clock untouched. For comparison NVENC on an RTX 4090 took 1.75-1.82 ms (p13).

power.note: hwmon power1_average with Steam's Big Picture and the stream running: within noise

gl_3d_check.note: manual DPM with only vclk/dclk set leaves the 3D clock free
